name: Vashti
overview: Vashti was a female figure known as the queen of Persia, as recorded in Esther 1:9. Beyond her royal title, Scripture provides no additional tribal or personal notes about her background. Her role is primarily defined by her position as queen during the reign of King Ahasuerus.
namesAndTitles: The name Vashti means 'one beautiful, desired,' highlighting her recognized beauty. She is also referred to by the title 'Queen Vashti,' which simply identifies her as the queen in the biblical narrative (Esther 1:9, 1:12). Neither name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Vashti as the wife of King Ahasuerus, as inferred from Esther 1:9. No further family relationships or tribal affiliations are recorded for her in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Vashti's significance in Scripture centers on her role as queen during a pivotal moment in the Persian empire under King Ahasuerus. Her position as queen establishes the backdrop for the unfolding events in the book of Esther, marking her as an important figure in the narrative's royal context. Though limited in detail, her presence helps set the stage for the biblical story of God's providence in a foreign kingdom.
